questions.question: Which of the following provision of the Indian constitution is **not **borrowed from the constitution of Britain?
questions.solution:
the correct answer __**Fundamental Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution is not borrowed from Britain; it's inspired by the US Constitution.**
 
• Fundamental Rights protect the** basic human rights of all citizens of India and are essential for the development of the individual and the country.**
 
• They include rights like equality** before the law, freedom of speech and expression, and protection from discrimination.**
 
• These rights can be **enforced by courts, and any law infringing them can be declared null and void.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Legislative procedure
 This process of making laws is borrowed from the British Constitution.
 
 

 Bicameralism
 The concept of a parliament divided into two houses, the Rajya Sabha (Upper House) and the Lok Sabha (Lower House), is borrowed from the British Constitution.
 
 

 Rule of law
 This principle that every person is subject to the law, including people who are lawmakers, government officials, and judges, is borrowed from the British Constitution.

questions.question: Certain plants have green and tender stems. They are usually short and may not have many branches. What are they called as?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Herbs are **small, seed-bearing plants with soft stems.**
 
• Certain plants have green and tender stems.
 
• They are usually short and may not have many branches.
 
• They are **shorter than shrubs or trees and generally do not have many branches.**
 
• Their green and tender stem differentiate them from other plant categories like trees or shrubs.
 
• Herbs usually have medicinal, culinary, or aromatic qualities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 **Option**
 **Description**
 
 
 
 

 Shrubs
 Medium-sized, woody plants that are taller than herbs but shorter than trees.
 
 

 Trees
 Large, woody plants with a single, sturdy stem or trunk and branches.
 
 

 Creepers
 Plants with weak stems cannot stand upright and spread over the ground or climb using other plants and structures for support.

questions.question: A megabyte (MB) consists of 1024 ______.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A Megabyte (MB)** is a unit of digital information storage or transmission with the prefix mega, denoting multiplication by** one million in decimal and by 1024 in binary.**
 
• The unit symbol for the **Megabyte is MB.**
 
• One megabyte is equal to **1024 kilobytes (KB).**
 
• This is based on the binary system of data storage used in computing.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Gigabytes
 One gigabyte (GB) is 1024 megabytes (MB).
 
 

 Terabytes
 One terabyte (TB) is 1024 gigabytes (GB).
 
 

 Bytes
 A byte is the basic unit of information storage and transmission in digital systems. One kilobyte (KB) is 1024 bytes.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of 'elements - valency' is correct?

I. Boron - 2

II. Fluorine -3
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fluorine** has a **valency of 1 **because it needs to gain only **one electron** to achieve a** stable electron configuration of 8 valence electrons.**
 
• **Boron** has a** valency of 3** because it tends to lose its** three valence electrons **to achieve a stable electron configuration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Valency,** also known as** oxidation number,** is a **measure of an element's combining capacity** or the** number of electrons it can gain, lose, or share when forming chemical compounds.**
 
• It determines** how an element will bond with other elements to form compounds.**
 
• The valency of an element is determined by the** number of valence electrons it possesses.**
 
• **Valence** electrons are the electrons present in the outermost energy level or shell of an atom.
 
• These electrons are involved in **chemical reactions** and have the potential to participate in** bonding**.

questions.question:
Which of the following assumptions is made to determine the level of aggregate demand for final goods in the economy?

I. A constant final goods price and constant rate of interest over short run are assumed.

II. The aggregate supply is assumed to be perfectly elastic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__ . 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assumption I, **which assumes a constant final goods price and a constant rate of interest over the short run, helps in** analyzing the relationship between aggregate demand and other macroeconomic variables such as consumption, investment, and government spending.**
 
• Assumption II, which assumes that aggregate supply is perfectly elastic, implies that firms can produce any quantity of goods and services at a given price level. This assumption simplifies the analysis of **aggregate demand and supply interactions in the economy.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The demand for final goods in an economy refers to the total quantity of finished **goods and services** that **consumers, businesses, and government entities **are** **willing and able to purchase at a given price level and during a specific period. 

 
 
• **Several factors influence the demand for final goods:**
 
• **Consumer Spending**
 
• **Business Investment**
 
• **Government Expenditure**
 
• **International Trade**
 
• **Monetary and Fiscal Policies**
 
• **Income Levels**

questions.question: Ain-i Akbari, a document on life of Mughal ruler Akbar does not contain information about ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ancestors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ain-i Akbari does not contain** information about Akbar's "**Ancestors**".
 
• The** Ain-i Akbari is the third volume of the Akbarnama, written by Abul Fazl, one of the Nine Gems (Navratnas) in Akbar's court.**
 
• This document offers a detailed account of **Akbar's reign, including his administration, the state's revenues, and the army.**
 
• However, it does not offer detailed information about his ancestors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The Akbarnama, in its first volume, does discuss Akbar's ancestors, but the **Ain-i Akbari, being the third volume, focuses more on Akbar's own reign and governance, not his lineage.**
 
• Th**e Ain-i Akbari is a five-part book which deals with the court, military establishment, the religions of the empire, the imperial administration, and the social conditions of the empire, among other aspects. It does not delve into the history of Akbar's ancestors.**
 
• The **focus of the Ain-i Akbari is more empirical and administrative, providing intricate details about Akbar's administration, army, and revenue collection.**
 
• **It provides detailed and accurate statistical data about various aspects of Mughal governance.**
 
• The Ain-i Akbari, unlike some other historical documents, isn't a genealogical record or a family history.
 
• **Its primary purpose was to document the empire under Akbar's reign.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Explanation
 
 
 
 

 Revenues
 
 
The Ain-i Akbari provides a detailed account of the state's revenues.

 
It describes the Mughal fiscal system, detailing the revenue of each province (subah), district, and village.

 
 
 

 Army
 
 
The Ain-i Akbari presents a detailed picture of the Mughal army, its structure, and its organization.

 
It provides an account of the rank and file in the Mughal military.

 
 
 

 Administration
 
 
The Ain-i Akbari provides comprehensive details about Akbar's administration, including the civil, judicial, and military administrations.

 
It details the bureaucratic structure and various administrative practices of the Mughal Empire under Akbar.

questions.question: The Sattriya dance form originated in which of the following Indian States?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Assam__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sattriya is the classical dance form of Assam.
 
• It was developed by the Vaishnavite saint and reformer Sankardeva in the 15th century.
 
• Sattriya is a combination of folk dances, martial arts, and classical Indian dance forms.
 
• It is characterized by its graceful movements, intricate footwork, and use of traditional Assamese costumes and music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• Sattriya was developed by the Vaishnavite saint and reformer Sankardeva in the 15th century.
 
• Sankardeva was a native of Assam, and he founded a number of monasteries in the region.
 
• Sattriya was originally performed in these monasteries as a way to spread Sankardeva's teachings.
 
• Sattriya is a combination of folk dances, martial arts, and classical Indian dance forms.
 
• This makes it a unique and distinctive dance form.
 
• Sattriya is characterized by its graceful movements, intricate footwork, and use of traditional Assamese costumes and music.
 
• These elements combine to create a beautiful and captivating dance form.
 
• Sattriya is a living tradition that is still performed today.

questions.question: India has won 8 olympic gold medals in which sport till 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Field Hockey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in "Field Hockey" till 2020.**
 
• Field Hockey is the sport in which **India has had the most success in the Olympics.**
 
• India won its first Olympic gold medal in field hockey in the** 1928 Amsterdam Olympics.**
 
• Following the **1928 **win, the Indian hockey team won gold in the **next five Olympics, continuing their winning streak until the 1956 Melbourne Olympics.**
 
• The **seventh gold medal **came at the **1964 Tokyo Olympics** and the **eighth at the 1980 Moscow Olympics.**
 
• Despite a long period of dominance in field hockey, **India's performance in this sport has waned in recent decades.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Olympic Games are an **international multi-sport event subdivided into summer and winter sporting events.**
 
• The games are considered the world's foremost sports competition,** with more than 200 nations participating.**
 
• The Olympics are held every four years, with the** Summer and Winter Games alternating every two years.**
 
• The modern Olympic Games were inspired by the ancient Olympic Games, which were held in **Olympia, Greece, from the 8th century BC to the 4th century AD.**
 
• **The International Olympic Committee (IOC)**, established in **1894**, has been the governing body of th**e Olympic Movement and oversees the planning of the Olympic Games.**
 
• The **Olympic motto is "Citius, Altius, Fortius," Latin for "Faster, Higher, Stronger," signifying the athletes' aspiration to push the boundaries of human performance.**
